summary: Customer reports overbilling when client disconnects during streaming responses (tokens continue accruing after disconnect)
description:
Issue summary
- Customer reports that for streaming chat completions, if their client disconnects mid-stream (mobile app backgrounded / proxy timeout), our invoice appears to include more output tokens than their app received.
- They see a higher token total on the invoice vs their internal counter (delta varies 3–9% depending on day), and believe we are billing for tokens after disconnect.

Impact
- Revenue risk: customer is threatening to dispute the latest invoice unless we can explain the delta and/or remediate.
- Trust risk: customer is using this as a procurement blocker for an expansion.

Customer details
- Company: Northbridge AI (enterprise)
- Workload: chat completions with streaming enabled; heavy mobile traffic; moderate concurrency (peaks ~120 req/min)
- Endpoint: /v1/chat/completions (stream=true)

Environment
- prod / us-east
- Observed since: ~2026-01-28 (customer noticed during Feb invoice preview)

What the customer is doing
- They open an SSE stream and terminate it when the user navigates away.
- They log tokens by counting deltas they received client-side.

Redwood expectation (per docs)
- We bill for tokens generated and delivered up to the point of disconnect.
- We should not bill tokens generated after the client disconnect signal is processed.

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Make a streaming request to /v1/chat/completions with a long max_tokens (e.g., 2048).
2) After receiving ~200–400 tokens, close the client connection.
3) Compare:
   a) gateway stream termination timestamp
   b) serving runtime generation timeline
   c) metering event token counts
   d) billing aggregate output tokens
4) Verify whether output tokens continue increasing after disconnect.

Evidence / logs (customer provided)
- Request IDs (sample):
  - req_01HT8NQ9K1Q7R7A9D8P7C6J2A1
  - req_01HT8NR3J9QX3B5K3T7F9G2ZQ4
- Customer notes: "We consistently see Redwood reporting ~80-150 extra output tokens on disconnect cases. This doesn’t happen when we run non-streaming."

Initial investigation notes (Support)
- This resembles the known streaming disconnect accounting bug where downstream metering counts tokens produced by the model even after client disconnect, instead of tokens successfully emitted.
- Potentially exacerbated by retries/proxy resets on the customer side.

Requested outcome
- Confirm whether this is a Redwood defect vs misunderstanding.
- Provide a written explanation and remediation plan (fix + backfill window).
- If overbilled, propose credit/refund amount and timing.

Customer comms template (draft for approval)
Subject: Update on streaming disconnect token accounting

Hi <Customer Name>,

We investigated the discrepancy you reported for streaming requests that disconnect mid-response. We confirmed an issue in our streaming accounting where output tokens could continue to be recorded after the client connection was terminated, even though those tokens were not delivered to your client.

What this means:
- For streaming requests that end due to client disconnects/timeouts, our billing system may have counted additional output tokens beyond what was actually streamed.
- Non-streaming requests are not impacted.

What we’re doing:
1) We have implemented a fix to stop token accounting at the disconnect boundary.
2) We are backfilling the affected period and will validate invoice totals against the corrected aggregates.
3) If the backfill shows you were overbilled, we will issue a credit on your next invoice (or refund if preferred), and we will share the calculation details.

Next steps:
- We will send you an update by <DATE> with the backfill results and the exact credit amount (if applicable).

Thank you for flagging this.
<Sender Name>
Redwood Inference Support

resolution: Root cause confirmed: streaming metering used runtime-generated output token count rather than tokens emitted before client disconnect, causing overcount for disconnect cases. Engineering shipped fix (PR 41903) to stop accounting at disconnect boundary and capture partial usage correctly. Ran backfill for 2026-01-20..2026-02-14 to regenerate billing aggregates. Finance approved issuing a credit memo to customer for the overbilled delta rather than reissuing the invoice. Customer notified with written explanation and timeline; dispute risk mitigated.
next_steps: Ensure hosted API meter definitions explicitly describe streaming disconnect behavior and billing boundary (docs alignment).
Add/keep dashboard and alert for disconnect_token_delta anomalies; suppress during planned backfills.
Confirm credit memo is applied on next invoice and recorded in billing dispute case log.
